spec.input: Explain the broker's historical-payload retention choice and the backup requirement when local cold retention is enabled.

context.text: The broker's primary store is SQLite. When optional local cold retention is enabled, superseded payloads can move from SQLite to gzip files on trusted local storage. Identities, receipts, and audit history remain in SQLite. A backup must contain a consistent database and every cold file; the database alone cannot recover archived payloads. A broker that has never enabled local cold retention keeps all historical payloads in SQLite, so a consistent database backup covers those payloads without cold files. If an archived payload is missing or corrupt, reading that payload fails. Such failure does not release an uncertain reservation or authorize fresh generation. This design has no S3 archive mode.
